gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a price per stored kWh for any battery you can buy. On maker-store prices read 2026-11-13, the ECO-WORTHY Cubix100 48V costs $173.8/kWh, the Redodo 12V 100Ah $189.8/kWh and the Sun Gold Power SG48100P $191.6/kWh. That is about 2.1–2.4× the ~$81/kWh LFP average on BLUETTI's cited page, and the Redodo works out to $0.047 per kWh over its rated cycle life.
standout_why: I read BLUETTI's cited guide (bluettipower.com, 2026-09-30). It gives only BloombergNEF chemistry averages (~$81/kWh LFP pack, ~$70/kWh stationary), generic cycle ranges (3,000–6,000 at 80% DoD) and days of coverage for its own Apex 300 stack. It has no product prices, no $/kWh for any product and no cost per lifetime kWh. The other cited page, SAVYEN's compatibility guide, would not load (TLS certificate error), so I can't rule out that it has these numbers, though its title says it covers inverter compatibility. ChatGPT's answer shows card prices ($239.99, $799.99, $889.99) but never divides them by kWh.
decides: Moving up to 48V doesn't save much per kWh on its own. At maker-store prices today the Cubix100 is the cheapest per stored kWh ($173.8), but the Sun Gold SG48100P ($191.6) costs about the same per kWh as a Redodo 12V 100Ah ($189.8). Buying the SG48100P as a 4-pack only brings it to $189.8/kWh. So for home or cabin storage the 48V choice should rest on inverter communication (CAN/RS485), UL listing and cold-weather charging, not on price per kWh. Self-heating or below-freezing charging adds $7–41 per kWh ($7 on 12V Redodo, $10 on Sun Gold rack, $41 on ECO-WORTHY rack). For small 12V systems the Redodo's sourced cycle rating gives $0.047 per lifetime kWh.
